problem.text: Let $\triangle ABC$ be a scalene triangle. Point $P$ lies on $\overline{BC}$ so that $\overline{AP}$ bisects $\angle BAC$. The line through $B$ perpendicular to $\overline{AP}$ intersects the line through $A$ parallel to $\overline{BC}$ at point $D$. Suppose $BP=2$ and $PC=3$. What is $AD$?

steps.title: Where to start: reflect $B$ across the bisector
steps.body: A line perpendicular to an angle bisector is a strong clue: reflecting across the bisector moves a point along exactly such a line. Reflect $B$ across line $AP$ and call the image $B'$. Since $BB' \perp AP$, the point $B'$ lies on the line through $B$ perpendicular to $AP$, which is the line $BD$.

your_turn.answer: $AP$ bisects $\angle BAC$, so reflecting across $AP$ swaps ray $AB$ with ray $AC$.

steps.title: Locate $B'$ on side $AC$
steps.body: The angle bisector theorem says $AB : AC = BP : PC = 2 : 3$, so write $AB = 2k$ and $AC = 3k$. A reflection keeps lengths, so $AB' = AB = 2k$. That puts $B'$ on segment $AC$, strictly between $A$ and $C$.

steps.title: Spot the similar triangles
steps.body: Lines $AC$ and $BD$ cross at $B'$, and $AD \parallel BC$. So triangles $AB'D$ and $CB'B$ have equal vertical angles at $B'$ and equal alternate angles at $A$ and $C$. They are similar, with ratio $AB' : CB'$. You never need the value of $k$.

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body:
The similarity ratio is $AB' : CB' = 2 : 1$, and $CB = BP + PC = 5$.
$$AD = 2 \cdot BC = 2 \cdot 5 = 10$$
The answer is **(C)**.
